episodes.title: Episode 27: The Pastor’s Wife | The Tragedy of Religious Trauma
episodes.description: Episode 27: The Pastor's Wife | The Tragedy of Religious Trauma When a church becomes control, love can turn into a trap. This conversation goes deep into the line between faith, manipulation, and the stories women are told to endure - especially when the people around them call it devotion. Ashley and Aqueelah start with pop-culture grief over Dolly Parton and Tim Curry, but the episode quickly pivots into a raw, urgent breakdown of The Death of the Pastor's Wife and the Allegedly (both on Netflix) episode on Pastor JP Miller. What begins as a documentary reaction becomes a powerful look at coercion, spiritual abuse, marriage, and the way systems can slowly convince someone they have no way out. You'll discover: ​Why Ashley sees the pastor's behavior as more than infidelity and more like psychological domination ​How Aqueelah's Allegedly deep dive changes the way she reads the documentary ​The role of church culture, submission, and “obedience” in keeping women trapped ​Why both hosts argue that women are often taught to confuse suffering with righteousness ​How “mental shackles” can make an open door feel closed ​What the conversation reveals about financial dependence, self-worth, and leaving before things get worse Ashley brings a sharp, uncompromising take on how women are conditioned to stay small, stay nice, and stay too long. Aqueelah adds the documentary context, emotional reaction, and the larger question of how faith communities can become environments of fear instead of care. This episode also widens out into a bigger critique of Christianity, particularly the way power, gender, and control are protected in the name of God. If you've ever wondered why some people stay in harmful relationships, or why “just leave” is never actually simple, this conversation will hit hard. Essential listening if you care about true crime, church culture, women's autonomy, emotional abuse, and the stories we tell ourselves to survive. It's honest, sharp, funny, painful, and impossible to ignore. | New episodes every Saturday. Follow us on Instagram @twothingscanbetrue.podcast and join the Group Chat.

episodes.title: Episode 16: The Cult of Nature Boy | Cults in the Black Community
episodes.description: Episode 16: The Cult of Nature Boy | Cults in the Black Community In 2017, a man named Eligio Bishop — known online as Nature Boy — was building a following inside a Black community that was grieving, afraid, and looking for safety. The world was giving them every reason to distrust the system. He used that. And it worked. This week, Aqueelah and Ashley break down the Hulu documentary The Cult of Nature Boy — the psychology behind why people join cults, why Black Americans were specifically vulnerable in that moment in history, and what the research says about the tactics used to pull people in and keep them there. Also Aqueelah shares something she's never talked about publicly. Something that could have gone differently and very left. Two things can be true: the community was not wrong about the world. They were wrong about him. Watch The Cult of Nature Boy on Hulu before or after — either way, let's talk about it. 📲 Come to the Group Chat. Drop your thoughts. We read everything. _______________ @ twothingscanbetrue.podcast
